method: Read every broker RPC (operation, args, ok/err) and every executor call result/response for all five packages; read full judge stream transcripts (tool calls, receipts, final structured judgment+feedback) for WC v3.1 and v3.3, LIT v3.1, WE v3.3 (v3.1 candidate compared), IDEA -004 v3.1; read the relevant H0 source (normalize_task, task_block, context_block, ACTIONS) and interface v4 text; independently recomputed WC word counts, WE embedded-CSV bytes vs published CSV (identical), WE manifest contents, LIT final-request context contents, EXP output design. execution.design_note: Executor ran every trajectory to 20000 iterations without early stop although median first-hit was 263-762 iterations, and retained every iterate (as the task requires) for 120 trajectories; this pushed replicate_results.jsonl above 128 MiB.

facts: The 128 MiB cap exists only in TaskView resources.artifact_collection; task.md never states it. The prompt's input contract lists cpus 2, memory 2048, disk_mb 1024, wall 1200 but not the cap (the executor copied exactly these into config.resource_budget), so it plausibly believed ~800 MiB of /work tmpfs was usable.
H0 renders 'RESOURCE LIMITS: {}' and 'CONSTRAINTS: {}' (V3-7): the harness had the cap in its TaskView; the executor never saw it.
quota_attribution.conclusion: Attributable to the harness under test, not the platform: primarily H0 V3-7 (published resource not relayed), proximately a genuine executor design choice (full 20000-iteration retention, no early stop) made without visibility of the cap. Not attributable to the executor alone. Secondary material issue: the package prose mandates per-iteration retention but omits the collection cap.

controller_handling.observed: Stage failed; no judge; failure.json preserves RPCs, executed entrypoints and platform log with hashes; artifact_status unknown_uncollected_or_incomplete; automatic_zero false; attribution pending_evidence_review; no retry; container removed.
controller_handling.vs_T06: Matches T06 as written: failure preserved, not silently dropped, not auto-zero, attribution left for review, no automatic retry.

No pre-registered fixed rule for a harness-caused collection-quota violation (7.5 says hard-budget violations follow fixed platform rules); the current rule yields no measurement rather than a scored violation. Needs a decision before formal runs.

Judges read subsets of platform traces (disclosed). No invented defects or leakage found in the 5 scored judgments, but each is a single run; stability not established (T03 open).

recommendations: Treat WC 3.75, IDEA 3.8, LIT 1.75, WE 3.0 as development H0-v3 measurements with the caveats above; do not use IDEA -002/-003 outcomes or v3.1 WC/IDEA-002 judge outcomes as agent evidence.
Add H0-NEW-A and H0-NEW-B to the H0 v3 defect register (recorded, not repaired); with V3-7 they are the main levers an evolver should discover from public feedback.

EXP: log as harness-attributable quota violation; before formal runs have the user fix a pre-registered rule (e.g., skip-and-record oversize files, collect remaining in-quota files, judge with a violation flag or fixed resource penalty) instead of whole-stage abort.
Materials: state the collection cap (and that /work tmpfs exceeds it) in task prose / input-contract resources for packages that mandate large per-iteration outputs (IV EXP especially).

Judge v3.3: require reading full-resolution tiles when image_delivery_downscaled is present, at least for legibility or 'all values match' claims; give WRITE_CONTENT an explicit word-count convention or a controller-computed count as evidence.
T03 remains open: these are single judge runs; they show plausible evidence-grounded grading and no observed leakage, not reliability.
limitations: Transcripts read via summarising scripts plus targeted full reads; judge thinking blocks were empty/redacted and not assessable.
No container re-execution; EXP numeric claims rest on in-run stdout only, and EXP artifacts were never collected.
Private reference contents were read only as delivered in judge receipts; their correctness was not re-audited.

Single run per package; no variance estimate; development evidence only.
